decision: Run Phase 1 against a real local Keycloak defined in docker-compose.yml, while keeping the identity provider a configuration value so the Sprint-1 provider decision stays open.
rationale: RF-01 forbids mock tokens anywhere including demo builds, and the API previously could not get past login because no Oidc:Authority was configured. A locally hosted Keycloak is a real OIDC provider validating against a real JWKS, so it satisfies both no-mock-tokens and demonstrate-end-to-end. The newest corpus document names Keycloak unambiguously as foundation component F7.
alternatives_considered: Config-only with no provider - rejected: leaves the feature undemonstrable while deferring a decision that does not need deferring, since the authority is configuration either way. A development token issuer - rejected: RF-01 forbids exactly that, including test and demo builds.

decision: The API returns which dashboard cards and table columns exist, in what order and with what labels; the Angular client renders whatever arrives and owns only the status-key to colour-triple mapping.
rationale: Foundation acceptance criterion 9 requires a second state to render without a frontend code change, and the previous design hardcoded the eight statuses in both a C# record and a TypeScript array. Colours stay client-side because the design system pairings are WCAG-checked constants; shipping them as rows would turn a contrast regression into something no build step can catch.
alternatives_considered: Fully server-driven including colours - rejected: converts an accessibility-checked constant into unvalidated runtime data. Client owns the card set with the server returning counts only - rejected: adding a status stays a frontend deploy, the exact thing criterion 9 tests.

decision: Discover CQRS handlers, validators and behaviours by scanning assemblies once at startup into a frozen registry, so the request path does no reflection and a missing or duplicated handler fails the host at startup.
rationale: The previous dispatcher called MakeGenericType and MethodInfo.Invoke on every dispatch and required a hand-written DI line per handler, so a handler that was never registered failed on the first request that needed it rather than at deployment. In a system where a skipped federal check and a passed one must never look alike, a silently unhandled request is the worst failure mode available.
alternatives_considered: Keep per-dispatch reflection - rejected: turns a missing handler into a production incident instead of a failed startup. Adopt MediatR - rejected: commercially licensed from v12 per config/architecture-baseline.json:95, and the needed surface is small; if a licence is purchased this decision should be superseded rather than defended.

decision: Isolate every Phase 1 seeded and synthetic implementation in a separate Cnp.SyntheticData project whose data lives in JSON files, and throw at registration when the environment is Production.
rationale: Synthetic data is permitted in Phase 1 but synthetic authentication is not, and the fabricated dashboard store previously sat inside Cnp.Api with its values as C# literals, distinguished from production code only by its name. A separate assembly makes the boundary a compiler-verified project reference, and JSON data means changing the demo does not require a build.
alternatives_considered: Keep it in Cnp.Api behind a config flag - rejected: a flag defaulted wrong serves fabricated participant data from a real deployment and looks like working software. Embed the data as resources - rejected: puts the demo dataset back behind a compiler, defeating the reason for moving it out of .cs files.

decision: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml in cnp-platform, taking the ORCHESTRATOR_ALLOW_GOVERNANCE_EDIT override for that filename.
rationale: config-protection denied the create because its governance patterns match the filename ci.yml on path alone, so it cannot distinguish CREATING a gate that adds enforcement from EDITING one to weaken it. Verified that cnp-platform has no .github directory and no workflow of any kind, so there is no gate to weaken: this adds the repository's first build, test, format and vulnerability-scan gate. Nothing existing is loosened. Same limitation already recorded as d-0003 on the hub repository.
alternatives_considered: Leave the repo with no CI - rejected: config/architecture-baseline.json:57 makes a ci-gate due before the first PR, and a gate that relies on people remembering is not a gate.

decision: The API returns typed view data - named status counts and typed application rows - and the Angular client owns all markup structure, with every component split into .ts, .html, .scss and .spec.ts.
rationale: Supersedes d-0002. Server-driven composition surrendered compile-time typing on both sides of the wire to buy variation the requirements never ask for: the eight statuses are fixed by the design system and several are federally fixed. Foundation acceptance criterion 9 names brand tokens, the OIDC realm and feature flags - not table columns - and all three still arrive from tenant config, so the criterion is unaffected.
alternatives_considered: Keep server-driven composition - rejected: untyped dictionary rows, markup structure decided in JSON, and two conventions for server-driven UI in one codebase. Keep column metadata for the table only - rejected: preserves the untyped rows, which is the worst part, for the smallest benefit.

decision: Superseded by d-0006 and ADR-0005: the API returns typed view data and the Angular client owns all markup structure.
rationale: Server-driven dashboard composition surrendered compile-time typing on both sides of the wire for variation the requirements do not ask for. See docs/adr/0005-typed-view-data-not-server-driven-html.md for the full argument, including why Foundation acceptance criterion 9 does not require it.
